name: NVIDIA Corporation
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: NVIDIA is this ecosystem's demand engine and architecture-setter — its rack-power roadmap (~120–150 kW GB300 racks today → ~600 kW Kyber racks with 800VDC in 2027 → 1 MW-class beyond) dictates what every power and storage supplier in the file must build, and its published 800VDC partner list is the de facto qualification slate for the next generation of data-center power. BACKGROUND: Founded 1993 by Jensen Huang; the dominant supplier of AI data-center compute (~80–85% of AI-accelerator revenue per IDC-cited estimates, down from ~92% in 2023). Fiscal years end late January: FY2026 (ended 2026-01-25) revenue was $215.9B (+65%), with the data-center segment at $193.7B. Q1 FY2027 revenue $81.6B (+85% YoY); Q2 FY2027 guided to $91B.
ecosystemRole: We assess NVIDIA as the ecosystem's gravitational center: it does not sell power or storage, but its architecture decisions create the market for both. Basis: the company itself prescribes a two-tier energy-storage hierarchy for AI factories — supercapacitors at the rack for millisecond GPU transients, and facility-level BESS at the utility interconnection for second-to-minute smoothing — and productized rack-level power smoothing in GB300 NVL72 (up to 30% peak-grid-demand reduction). Its 800VDC ecosystem list names the power vendors (Delta, LITEON, Megmeet, Flex among components; Vertiv, Eaton, Schneider, Siemens, ABB, GE Vernova, Hitachi Energy at the grid tier) who will carry the 2027 transition.

productsAndServices.name: Rack-Scale AI Compute Platforms (Blackwell → Rubin → Feynman)
productsAndServices.description: Full-rack AI systems: GB200/GB300 NVL72 (72 Blackwell-class GPUs + 36 Grace CPUs, 130 TB/s NVLink domain, liquid-cooled), Vera Rubin NVL72/NVL144 (production 2H 2026; 100% liquid-cooled MGX racks, ~3.6 EFLOPS FP4 per NVL144 per keynote figures), Rubin Ultra NVL576 in Kyber racks (2H 2027, ~600 kW/rack, 15 EFLOPS FP4), and the announced Feynman generation (Kyber NVL1152, co-packaged optics, 1 MW-class racks). GTC 2026 added the Groq 3 LPU/LPX inference rack to the platform line-up.
highlights: Rack power trajectory is the ecosystem's forcing function: >200 kW today → ~600 kW (Kyber, 2H 2027) → '1 MW IT racks and beyond' (company-stated architecture target)
GB300 NVL72 productized power smoothing: ~65 J/GPU energy storage in power shelves, ramp control, and 'GPU burn' — cutting peak grid demand up to 30% (NVIDIA-published)
Cloud GPUs 'sold out' per Huang (Q3 FY2026); supply commitments jumped from $50.3B to $95.2B in one quarter (Q4 FY2026 filing)
GB300 platform estimated at 70–80% of 2026 AI rack shipments (TrendForce), with Vera Rubin ramping 2H 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: Holds ~80–85% of data-center AI-accelerator revenue (IDC-cited estimates); AMD Instinct ~5–7%; hyperscaler custom silicon (TPU/Trainium/Maia/MTIA) ~10–20% of revenue and growing faster, concentrated in inference. Four direct customers were 61% of Q3 FY2026 revenue per the 10-Q — concentration is structural.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: ODM/CSP intermediaries (direct customers) serving hyperscalers, NVIDIA Cloud Partners, sovereign AI programs, and enterprises
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscalers, neoclouds, frontier labs, sovereign AI, enterprise AI factories
productsAndServices.roadmap: Vera Rubin production 2H 2026; Rubin Ultra NVL576/Kyber + full 800VDC in 2H 2027; Feynman generation announced at GTC 2026

productsAndServices.name: 800VDC Power Architecture Initiative
productsAndServices.category: Ecosystem architecture · directly shapes this app's supplier coverage
productsAndServices.description: NVIDIA's facility-power redesign for 1 MW-class racks: grid 13.8 kV AC → 800 VDC distribution → single-stage conversion to 12 VDC at the compute node, replacing 415/480 VAC three-phase plus in-rack 54V conversion. Published claims: ~157% more power through the same copper vs 415 VAC, up to 45% copper reduction (a 1 MW rack carries up to 200 kg of busbar on legacy architecture), up to 5% end-to-end efficiency gain, −30% TCO. Full-scale production coincides with Kyber racks in 2027.
highlights: Named partner slate (May + Oct 2025 lists): power components — Delta, LITEON, Flex, Bizlink, Lead Wealth, **Megmeet**; DC power systems — ABB, Eaton, GE Vernova, Heron Power, Hitachi Energy, Mitsubishi Electric, Schneider, Siemens, Vertiv; silicon — Infineon, TI, Navitas, onsemi, ST and others
NVIDIA prescribes storage in the architecture itself: supercapacitors rack-side for millisecond transients, facility-level BESS at the interconnection for second-to-minute smoothing
Vertiv 800VDC MGX portfolio launching 2H 2026; Eaton reference architecture released Oct 2025; Foxconn's 40 MW Kaohsiung-1 cited as first 800VDC-ready facility

BBU/supercapacitor attach economics: AI-server BBU market ~$2.8B in 2026 → ~$7.1B by 2033 (analyst est.); each GB300 cabinet ~5 BBU modules + >300 supercapacitors, with supercap supply a genuine bottleneck (trade-press analysis)
productsAndServices.positioning: The de facto standards body for AI-factory power — OCP-aligned, whitepaper-published. Delta holds an estimated ~70% of Blackwell-platform AI-server PSUs (KGI), LITEON #2; Megmeet's inclusion in both partner lists is the mainland-China exception.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Open ecosystem: reference architectures + whitepaper; partners commercialize the hardware
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Data-center power vendors, grid-equipment OEMs, hyperscale facility designers
productsAndServices.roadmap: Full-scale 800VDC production with Kyber in 2027; industry 1 MW-rack adoption projected from ~2027

productsAndServices.name: Networking, Software & Other Platforms
productsAndServices.description: NVLink scale-up (130 TB/s per 72-GPU domain; NVLink-6 with Rubin), Spectrum-X/Spectrum-6 Ethernet, Quantum InfiniBand, ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, BlueField-4 DPUs — networking revenue reached $11.0B in Q4 FY2026 alone. Software: CUDA, NIM microservices, Nemotron open-model coalition, Omniverse. Automotive/physical AI: robotaxi platforms with BYD, Hyundai, Nissan, Geely; robotics partnerships (ABB, KUKA, Universal Robots).
highlights: Networking is the quiet second franchise — $11.0B in Q4 FY2026 (~16% of the quarter)
CUDA remains the moat argument analysts cite against custom-silicon substitution
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Same ODM/CSP channel plus direct enterprise software licensing

recentDevelopments.headline: 800VDC architecture unveiled at Computex with initial partner list (Delta, LITEON, Megmeet, Eaton, Schneider, Vertiv, Infineon, TI among named)
recentDevelopments.read: The founding document of the 2027 power transition this app's supplier dossiers orbit around.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess NVIDIA has converted its compute roadmap into control of the data-center power agenda: by publishing the 800VDC architecture, naming the qualified vendor slate, and prescribing storage placement (rack supercaps + interconnection BESS), it sets the requirements every power/BESS supplier in this app must meet for the 2027 Kyber generation. Basis: NVIDIA's own technical blogs and whitepaper.

(High confidence) We assess demand is now denominated in gigawatts: OpenAI (10 GW LOI), Anthropic (up to 1 GW initial), and >1.7 GW already deployed across NVIDIA Cloud Partners. Third-party projections of ~233 GW of cumulative new AI data-center power demand 2025–2030 rest heavily on NVIDIA's shipment cadence — the single most important demand variable for this ecosystem.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the circular-financing critique is the most serious structural risk: up to $100B invested in OpenAI as it buys NVIDIA systems, reported discussions of guaranteeing up to $250B of OpenAI lease payments, and four direct customers at 61% of revenue. Bernstein and Bloomberg Intelligence analysts flag it; Burry's depreciation-understatement thesis (~$176B, 2026–2028) is the bear case NVIDIA felt compelled to rebut directly.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the GB300 power-smoothing feature set (rack energy storage, ramp control, up to 30% peak-demand reduction) partially internalizes what would otherwise be BESS-supplier revenue — but simultaneously legitimizes storage-at-the-rack, expanding the BBU/supercapacitor market (~$2.8B → ~$7.1B by 2033 per analyst estimates) faster than it cannibalizes it.

(High confidence) China is now regulatory downside only: guidance assumes zero China data-center compute revenue after the H20 whipsaw ($4.5B charge, then a 15%-of-revenue export deal, then Beijing's effective blacklisting), and the SAMR Mellanox probe carries a potential ~$2.9B fine. Basis: filings, Commerce testimony, SAMR announcements.
